description: OPEM is the ECSIM team's open Python software for evaluating proton-exchange membrane fuel-cell performance. It implements several static and dynamic formulations, including models of individual stacks and selected auxiliary processes. Inputs include gas pressure and composition, cell temperature, current, active area and membrane thickness; outputs include calculated performance curves and HTML, CSV or OPEM-format reports. Coverage is equipment-level and user-configured, without a fixed geographic or observation period. Public source, command-line use and library examples are free under MIT. A limitation is that the available formulations represent different physical assumptions and sometimes particular stacks, so parameter choices and model applicability must be checked before comparing results. OPEM can supply fuel-cell performance calculations for hydrogen-to-electricity and backup-power simulations, complementing system-level PyPSA (model-pypsa). The repository documents input units and cites the 2018 JOSS software paper and underlying model literature. No equipment test data or executable package was downloaded.
